newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil says adjusts Aug Statfjord oil l.
newsitem.headline: Statoil says adjusts Aug Statfjord oil l.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeseselskap AS (Statoil) said on Thursday it had adjusted the August loading programme for Statfjord crude oil due to unscheduled shutdowns at the Statfjord C and Snorre platforms and generally lower-than-forecast production at the field.
Trading sources said on Thursday that August liftings of Statfjord crude had been put back by three days and two of the originally scheduled 28 cargoes had been deferred to September.

"The change to the programme is mainly due to Snorre's shutdown last week and a one-day shutdown at the Statfjord C platform, when we had to close the Statfjord North and East satellites as well," a Statoil spokesman said.
"The Statfjord C shutdown was not scheduled in our main maintenance plan."
Statfjord pumps around 157,000 barrels per day (bpd), while Statfjord East and North have a throughput of 67,000 bpd and 85,500 bpd respectively.
The 200,000 bpd Snorre platform was closed for five days last week after a short circuit caused a power black out.
Saga Petroleum, operator of Snorre, plans to have a three-day turnaround at Snorre from August 25. A spokesman for the company said the shutdown was not linked to recent problems at the field.
